newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower, awaits GCA stock data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower, awaits GCA stock data.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended lower in seesaw dealings on Monday, pressured by a late-session bout of speculative selling, floor sources said.

The benchmark March contract took a downturn this morning, breaching near-term support at 110.00 cents a lb and touching off sell-stops, traders said. But the day's low of 108.50 provided strong support, prompting locals to cover their short positions.
Trade and commission house buying pushed prices higher around midsession, dealers said, but March ran into resistance at the day's high of 112.50 and quickly came off.
"It hit a wall and dropped back more than 2.00 cents," one trader said.
March futures ended at 109.95 cents, down 1.25 cents, after ranging from 112.50 to 108.50. May fell 0.90 cent, to 107.40, while the back months shed 0.75 to 1.25 cents.
The December contract posted the steepest losses, diving 4.90 cents, to end at 124.50 cents. The December/March switch narrowed to 14.55 cents from 18.20 at the close Friday.
Traders await the U.S. Green Coffee Association of New York's November consumer coffee stock figures due after today's close.

Most traders expected stocks to continue to decline in November, with estimated decreases ranging from 100,000 to 300,000 60-kg bags. In October, GCA reported coffee stored in U.S. warehouses fell by 351,000 bags, to 1,260,000 bags, their lowest level since the GCA began tracking inventories in January, 1988.

The weekly CSCE certified coffee stock data is also due after today's close. As of Friday, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks stood at 2,321 bags in the week ended December 6. In addition, another 10,250 bags were certified for delivery sometime between December 9-13, and a further 18,500 bags were reported pending grading.
